business_name: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
offer_text: Locals, this one's for you: pay-what-you-want admission if you live in Davidson or a bordering county (Cheatham, Robertson, Rutherford, Sumner, Williamson, Wilson) — any amount, even zero, and youth 18 and under always walk in free.

The old post office turned art house never charges anyone 18 and under, and college students with a valid ID slip in free on Thursday and Friday evenings, 5 to 9 p.m. — the quietest, best-lit hours in the building.
Carry a Bank of America or Merrill card? Cheekwood honors the Museums on Us program with free general admission the first full weekend of every month — walk the mansion and the gardens on the house.
Nashville's full-scale Athena keeps her doors open to everyone: show an EBT card at the ticket counter through the Museums for All program and admission is free for up to four in your party.
Slide into the Germantown taproom on a weekday between 4 and 6 and it's $2 off every draft pour — the cleanest way to work through their hazy IPA lineup before the after-work crowd finds it.
No cover, ever — real honky-tonk seven days a week on Lower Broadway, and six dollars still buys the legendary Recession Special: fried bologna sandwich, chips, a Moon Pie, and a cold PBR.
Grab a Zanies t-shirt and you've bought yourself free admission to New Material Mondays for good — the night the road-tested headliners come in to try out the jokes that aren't ready yet.
Military and AAA members save 10% on backstage tours and select show tickets — bring valid ID to the box office, though note the discount can't be stacked on tour-plus-show combo packages.
Verified military members take 10% off Tier 2 seating on any midday or evening paddle-wheel cruise down the Cumberland — a standing thank-you, though it sits out the specialty holiday sailings.
Join the free Barista Bar Rewards+ app and your first drink's on them, plus one every birthday and a free 10th pour on the punch card — bring a reusable cup and you earn double stamps toward it.
Tennessee's first Natural Area asks nothing at the gate — free admission and free parking, every day. Come before 7 a.m. on a weekend to land a spot and catch the mist coming off the water.
